C0.quote: Social decision schemes (SDSs) map the ordinal preferences of individual voters
C0.note: Axiomatic study of randomized voting rules (SDSs), including strategyproofness and participation.

C1.quote: there is no Condorcet-consistent SDS that satisfies PC -strategyproofness
C1.note: Impossibility theorems; strategyproofness and participation are incentive properties. The efficiency-path result is also axiomatic/conceptual.

C2.2.note: Strict preferences; ties are not allowed.

C2.3.quote: We assume that the voters' preferences over alternatives are lifted to preferences over lotteries
C2.3.note: Voters have preferences over alternatives and lotteries.

C2.4.quote: no voter can benefit by lying about his true preferences
C2.4.note: Strategyproofness treats reported and true preferences as separate objects (R and R'), although the profile is also called preferences.

C3.1.quote: Intuitively, strategyproofness demands that no voter can benefit by lying
C3.1.note: Strategyproofness and participation analyses consider misreporting; the PC-efficiency and Proposition 5 analysis evaluates the profile as given.

C3.2.note: Efficiency is defined on the profile without any statement that voters report truthfully. Sections checked: 2, 4, 5.

C4.1.note: Voter utility is not used as such. The PC extension is defined on ordinal preferences, and expected utility is only mentioned for SD in the background.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used, except in a reference title.

C5.1.quote: we say a lottery p is X -efficient in R if it is not X -dominated
C5.1.note: PC-efficiency and Pareto efficiency are formal criteria in the results (Theorems 2 and 3, Proposition 5).

C5.2.quote: p is an X -improvement of q if p makes every voter weakly better off
C5.2.note: Efficiency is evaluated on the profile of preferences. There is no statement relating it to held versus reported preferences.
